conditions.summary: Pre-commencement land contamination site investigation and remediation scheme
conditions.text: No works pursuant to this permission shall commence until there has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority:- (a) a site investigation report documenting the ground conditions of the site and incorporating chemical and gas analysis identified as being appropriate by the desk study in accordance with BS10175:2011- Investigation of Potentially Contaminated Sites - Code of Practice; and, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority, (b) a detailed scheme for remedial works and measures to be undertaken to avoid risk from contaminants/or gases when the site is developed. The scheme must include a timetable of works and site management procedures and the nomination of a competent person to oversee the implementation of the works.

conditions.summary: Verification of contamination remediation scheme prior to occupation
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied/brought into use until there has been submitted to the Local Planning Authority verification by the competent person approved under the provisions of condition 4(b) that any remediation scheme required and approved under the provisions of condition 4(b) has been implemented fully in accordance with the approved details (unless varied with the written agreement of the Local Planning Authority in advance of implementation). Such verification shall comprise; i. as built drawings of the implemented scheme; ii. photographs of the remediation works in progress; iii. Certificates demonstrating that imported and/or material left in situ is free of contamination.

conditions.summary: Landscaping scheme to be submitted and approved prior to above slab level works

The works approved shall be carried out in the first planting and seeding seasons following the first occupation of the building(s) or when the use hereby permitted is commenced. Any trees or plants which, within a period of 5 years from the date of planting, die, are removed or become seriously damaged or diseased shall be replaced in the next planting season with others of similar size and species, to be agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Wildlife Protection and Mitigation Plan required prior to development
conditions.text:
No development, including any demolition works, soil moving, temporary access construction/widening, or storage of materials, shall commence until a Wildlife Protection and Mitigation Plan has been submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The plan shall include the wildlife mitigation measures given in Section 7 of Ecological Survey Ltd's Preliminary Ecological Appraisal dated January 2021.
No development or other operations shall take place other than in complete accordance with the approved Wildlife Protection and Mitigation Plan. No habitat or other landscape features that are to be retained as part of the approved Wildlife Protection and Mitigation Plan shall be damaged, destroyed or removed without the prior written approval of the Local Planning Authority, for the duration of activities permitted by this planning permission.
If a habitat or other landscape feature is removed or damaged in contravention of this condition, a scheme of remedial action, with a timetable for implementation, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority within 28 days of the incident.

The development shall be carried out and thereafter maintained in accordance with the details so approved. The details shall include: The recommendations given in Section 7 of Ecological Surveys Ltd's Preliminary Ecological Appraisal dated January 2021; The proposals for on-site habitat creation and enhancement to achieve the biodiversity net gain as shown in the submitted DEFRA biodiversity offsetting metric (including sources of planting stock and its origin); The provision of arrangements to secure the delivery of the offsetting measures (including a timetable for their delivery); and A management and monitoring plan (to include for the provision and maintenance of the submitted offsetting measures in perpetuity).

conditions.summary: Unacceptable scale, bulk and massing – harmful to character and streetscene
conditions.text: The proposal, by virtue of its scale, bulk and massing, would not be sympathetic to the character and visual quality of the area. The proposed scheme fails to have due regard to the scale, layout and appearance of the surrounding area, and the relationship to neighbouring buildings and landscape features. It fails to positively contribute to local distinctiveness, and the sense of place and would appear incongruous within the existing streetscene and cramped within the site. The development cannot be successfully integrated or mitigated within the landscape and surroundings. Accordingly, the proposal is contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (September 2023) and Policies EM1 and EM10 of the Basingstoke and Deane Local Plan 2011-2029.

conditions.summary: Harmful impact on boundary and category B trees – loss detrimental to character
conditions.text: The proposed development would put pressure on the future health and retention of the boundary trees which are considered to be important features in the local landscape. In addition, the scheme would result in the loss of a number of category B trees which add to the character of the area and there is insufficient space on site to seek replacement trees. The loss of trees would detrimentally impact the character and appearance of the surrounding area. Accordingly, the proposal is contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (September 2023), criteria b) and e) of Policy EM1 of the Basingstoke and Deane Local Plan 2011-2029, and the Landscape, Biodiversity and Trees Supplementary Planning Document 2018.

conditions.summary: Unacceptable impact on AWE Aldermaston DEPZ emergency planning arrangements
conditions.text: The application site is situated within the Detailed Emergency Planning Zone (DEPZ) surrounding the Aldermaston Atomic Weapons Establishment (AWE). The proposed development would as a result of the associated increase in population, proximity to the centre of the DEPZ and location within a densely populated sector of the DEPZ, have a detrimental impact on the Aldermaston off-site emergency planning arrangements in terms of response and recovery. The proposed emergency response plan is considered to be insufficient. As such the proposal would be contrary to the requirements of Policy SS7 of the Basingstoke and Deane Local Plan 2011-2029 and guidance contained within the National Planning Policy Framework (September 2023).

conditions.summary: Harmful overbearing and overlooking impact on No.8 Mulfords Hill residential amenity
conditions.text: As a result of the proximity of the proposed building to the adjacent dwelling (No.8 Mulfords Hill) the proposed development would result in a harmful impact on the amenity of this neighbour. The development would result in a dominant and overbearing experience for No.8 Mulfords Hill, causing an intrusive, oppressive and claustrophobic effect on their living conditions, which would result in a loss of privacy and outlook from their dwelling and garden. The resultant impact would be to significantly reduce the residential amenities of No.8 Mulfords Hill to a level below what may reasonably be expected in this location. Accordingly, the proposed development is contrary to Policy EM10 of the Basingstoke and Deane Local Plan 2011-2029 and Section 10 (Residential Amenity) of the Design and Sustainability Supplementary Planning Document (2018).

conditions.summary: Absence of legal agreement securing a Travel Plan
conditions.text: In the absence of any suitable legal agreement, or justification for the absence of a legal agreement, the proposed development does not make adequate provision for a Travel Plan. The proposed development is therefore contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework 2023; Policies CN6 and CN9 of the Basingstoke and Deane Local Plan 2011-2029, the Planning Obligations for Infrastructure Supplementary Planning Document 2018, and the Community Infrastructure Levy Regulations 2010 (as amended).

conditions.summary: Insufficient information on ecological impact of surface water drainage on adjacent SSSI
conditions.text: Insufficient information has been submitted with which to assess the full ecological impact of surface water drainage on the adjacent Pamber Forest and Silchester Common SSSI. Consequently, the submission is considered lacking in essential information and the development would be contrary to the guidance set out within Section 15 of the National Planning Policy Framework (September 2023), Policy EM4 of the Basingstoke and Deane Local Plan 2011-2029, Section 5 of the Landscape, Biodiversity, Trees Supplementary Planning Document (December 2018) and the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017.

conditions.summary: Inadequate on-site vehicular and cycle parking provision
conditions.text: The proposal would not provide adequate on-site vehicular parking for ten vehicles to serve the property and no cycle parking provisions have been made. As a result, the proposed development could result in the displacement of parking onto the highway, obstructing and causing undue interference with the convenience of users of the highway. There are no other material considerations that would address these harms. As such the proposed development is contrary to Policies CN9 and EM10 of the Basingstoke and Deane Local Plan 2011-2029 and the Basingstoke and Deane Parking Supplementary Planning Document July 2018.

conditions.summary: Insufficient information on visibility splays and highway safety
conditions.text: Due to the insufficient information provided to support the application with respect to the level of visibility splays and highway safety, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the amended rear parking area together with the proposal to widen the dropped kerb (on Wessex Close) would not result in an unacceptable level of risk to the motorists and other highway users, contrary to of highway safety Policy CN9 of the Basingstoke and Deane Local Plan 2011-2029 and the Basingstoke and Deane Parking Supplementary Planning Document July 2018.

conditions.summary: Lack of information on refuse and recycling storage and collection
conditions.text: Due to the lack of information on refuse and recycling storage and collection, the application has failed to demonstrate that there is adequate provision for refuse/recycle storage and safe collection points on site contrary to Policy CN9 of the Basingstoke and Deane Local Plan 2011-2029 and the Basingstoke and Deane Parking Supplementary Planning Document July 2018.

conditions.summary: Increased flood risk from additional hardstanding – no flood risk assessment
conditions.text: The site falls within an area which has potential to increase flooding as it falls within an area at risk of surface water flooding and falls within an area with a history of flooding. Due to the increase in the amount of hardstanding surface area resulting from the proposed extended Wessex Close parking area and enlarged dropped kerb (to the rear of the property), the proposal would result in an increase in the risk of flooding. No flood risk assessment has been provided to support the proposal and thus the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the proposal would not result in increased risk of flooding within the immediate surrounding area, contrary to Policy EM7 of the Basingstoke and Deane Local Plan 2011-2029.

conditions.summary: Inadequate outdoor amenity space for future HMO occupants
conditions.text: Given the size of the existing outdoor amenity space at the property, the proposal would not provide adequate amenity space for the enjoyment of the future occupants of the HMO. The harm would be exacerbated by the reduction in the size of the existing limited private amenity space due to the proposed extension of the existing rear parking space on Wessex Close, and further by the existing shortage of public outdoor amenity space within the immediate and wider area. This is contrary to Policy EM10 of the Basingstoke and Deane Local Plan 2011-2029 and the Design and Sustainability Supplementary Planning Document (2018).

conditions.summary: Refusal: inappropriate Green Belt development, no very special circumstances
conditions.text: The proposed development is not considered to comply with any exception set out at paragraphs 154 or 155 of the NPPF 2024, and therefore is considered to be inappropriate development in the Green Belt. The benefits of the development including the provision of housing, including 50% affordable housing, compliance with the Golden Rules set out at paragraphs 156 and 157 of the NPPF, provision of land for a care home, provision of land for a neighbourhood centre and associated economic benefits, flood risk betterment, and provision of open space, sports pitches and associated community building, are not considered to clearly outweigh the harms arising. The harms identified include definitional harm to the Green Belt, harm to Green Belt openness, conflict with Green Belt purpose (a), landscape harm, failure of the Flood Risk Sequential Test, and the loss of Best and Most Versatile agricultural land. As such, there are no very special circumstances that would justify the grant of planning permission as set out at paragraph 143 of the NPPF. The scheme would fail to comply with the NPPF (2024), Policy SADM26 of the Site Allocations and Development Management Policies Plan (2016) and Policy CS13 of the Core Strategy (2013). Accordingly planning permission is refused.

If the tree is removed, uprooted, destroyed, or be caused to die, or become seriously damaged or defective, within five years of planting, it shall be replaced with a tree of the same species and size and in an agreed location, in the first available planting season following removal.

Reason: To mitigate for the impact on the protected trees within the site. In accordance with policies CS12 of the Core Strategy 2013 and SADM12 of the Site Allocations and Development Management Policies Plan 2016.

conditions.summary: External materials to match existing building
conditions.text:
The materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted shall match those used in the existing building unless otherwise approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: To ensure that the finished appearance of the development will enhance the character and visual amenities of the area. To comply with Policy SADM30 of the Site Allocations and Development Management Policies Plan 2016, Policies SP1 and CS22 of the Hertsmere Core Strategy 2013 and the NPPF.

conditions.summary: Operational plant noise limit – 10dB(LAeq) below background at nearest residential
conditions.text:
Noise from plant and equipment associated with the development shall be 10dB (LAeq) below the background noise level (LA90) at the nearest residential properties (5dB below the background noise level if evidence is provided which shows that no tonality is present).

Reason: To protect the amenity of residents in the locality as required by polices SP1 and CS16 of the Core Strategy 2013, policy SADM20 of the Site Allocations and Development Management Policies Plan 2016 and the NPPF.

conditions.summary: Bat protection mitigation measures to be implemented during construction
conditions.text:
During construction of the development hereby approved, the mitigation measures to protect bats set out in the PRA Letter Report-Rev01 (Ref. TT4209), dated 22nd April 2025 shall be implemented in full.

Reason: To allow the LPA to discharge its duties under the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017 (as amended), the Wildlife & Countryside Act 1981 (as amended) and s40 of the NERC Act 2006 (Priority habitats & species) and to comply with policies SP1 and CS12 of the Core Strategy 2013 and SADM10 of Site Allocations and Development Management Policies Plan 2016.

applications.address: 8 - 9 Station Close Potters Bar Hertfordshire EN6 1TL
applications.description: Change of use from existing warehouse (Use Class B8) to provision of medical or health services (Use Class E(e)) and erection of cycle store.

conditions.summary: Inappropriate use in designated employment area — contrary to Policies CS8, CS10 and SADM5
conditions.text: The proposed development would result in the provision of an inappropriate use within a designated employment area and would undermine and be harmful to the function of the designated employment area. No employment land need assessment or similar has been submitted to justify the proposal. The development would thereby be contrary to Policies CS8 and CS10 of the Hertsmere Core Strategy 2013 and Policies SADM5 of the Site Allocations and Development Management Policies Plan 2016.

applications.address: Littledene Care Home 54 Bushey Grove Road Bushey Hertfordshire WD23 2JJ
applications.description: Variation of condition 1 to allow for broadening of the use of the existing care home property (Use Class C2) to include provision of care for children with learning difficulties following grant of planning permission 21/1287/VOC and TP/86/0038 (additional information received on 18.11.2025).

conditions.summary: Restriction of use to specified C2 care home purposes only
conditions.text: The premises shall be used for the provision of residential accommodation and care to adults in need of care by reason of old age, disablement or dementia, and children in need of care by reason of learning difficulties, and for no other purpose within Class C2 of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987, as amended, without the consent in writing of the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Maximum capacity limits for children's home and other C2 uses
conditions.text: The premises shall operate at a maximum capacity of 8-bedrooms when in use as a children's home for children in need of care by reason of learning difficulties, with all other permitted Class C2 uses of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 as amended, may operate to a maximum capacity of 14-bedrooms, unless prior consent is obtained in writing from the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Compliance with submitted Operational Management Plan (2025)
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in strict accordance with the recommendations and arrangements, as set out within the submitted Operational Management Plan (dated 2025).

conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in complete accordance with the approved plans and drawings listed in this decision notice, other than where those details are altered pursuant to the conditions of this planning permission. applications.description: Retention of single story flat roofed outbuilding with proposed additional landscaping and continued use as a Restaurant and use of existing Hotel parking (Retrospective).

conditions.summary: Inappropriate development in Green Belt – harmful to openness
conditions.text: The proposal constitutes inappropriate development in the Green Belt due to the scale of the building over and above the size of the previous garage block and as such, is considered to materially harm the openness of the Green Belt. There are no very special circumstances which outweigh this harm and therefore, the proposal is contrary to the NPPF 2024, Policy CS13 of the Hertsmere Core Strategy 2013 and SADM26 of the Site Allocations and Development Management Policies Plan 2016.

conditions.summary: Development to commence within 3 years of permission date
conditions.text:
The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of 3 years from the date of this permission.
Reason: To comply with the requirements of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

conditions.summary: Bicycle parking to be provided prior to first occupation and retained
conditions.text:
Prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved, the bicycle parking facilities shall be provided in accordance with the approved plans and shall thereafter be retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development.
Reason: To ensure a choice of sustainable transport options are provided for future occupiers. In accordance with Policies SP1, CS22, CS25, CS26 of the Hertsmere Local Plan Core Strategy (2013), Policies SADM30 and SADM40 of the Site Allocations and Development Management Policies Plan (2016) and the National Planning Policy Framework.

conditions.summary: Car parking spaces to be provided prior to first occupation and retained
conditions.text:
Prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved, the car parking spaces shall be provided in accordance with the approved plans and shall thereafter be retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development.
Reason: To accord with Policies CS22, CS24, CS25 of the Hertsmere Local Plan Core Strategy (2013), Policy SADM40 of the Site Allocations and Development Management Policies Plan (2016) and the National Planning Policy Framework.
